output.brief: The remote promotion gap is mostly a tenure effect, not proximity bias. Promotion requires 18 months in level, and only about 32% of remote staff meet that, versus about 74% of office staff. Among employees who are eligible, remote and office promotion approval rates are nearly identical (20.0% vs 21.1%), and nominations are similar (28.2% vs 28.6%). The per-job-family gaps in the dashboard do not show the bias either. Proximity bias is not proven, and the data cannot rule out a small true difference of a few points. The COO's three-day office rule would likely penalise remote staff, many of whom were hired on home-based contracts, for a gap that mostly reflects how recently they were hired. I'd not announce it. Next steps: re-run the promotion comparison among eligible staff only, and check why remote staff have less time in level (recent hiring or attrition, which I did not examine). Separately, review how stretch assignments are allocated, since the manager interviews raise that question but the data do not yet test it. Confidence is moderate. I reviewed only one of the two extra records I was allowed.
